title: Lesson 53 - Architectural Choices: Fitting OmniStudio into the Enterprise Landscape
description: Justify and recommend architectural choices, demonstrating how OmniStudio components fit into the overall Salesforce and enterprise system landscape.

questions.question: An architect is asked to replace a Visualforce page that guides a user through a five-step application with a guided flow that reads and writes Salesforce records. Which recommendation is the best fit?
options: A custom Lightning Web Component with a state machine
An OmniScript with Data Mappers for the reads and writes
A FlexCard embedded on the record page
An Apex batch job that processes the application
questions.explanation: An OmniScript is purpose-built for guided, stateful user journeys and reads and writes records under the user's context, which matches the requirement. A Lightning Web Component would require hand-built state management and offers no advantage here. A FlexCard is for embedded display, not multi-step input. An Apex batch job is for background processing, not interactive guidance.

questions.question: A solution needs a read-only summary of a customer's open cases displayed on the account record page. The data is already in Salesforce. What is the best fit?
options: An OmniScript that queries the cases on load
An Integration Procedure called from a custom component
A FlexCard with a Data Raptor that reads the cases
A scheduled Apex job that writes the summary to a field
questions.explanation: A FlexCard is designed for embedded, read-only display and a Data Raptor reads the cases directly from Salesforce, which is the lightest correct fit. An OmniScript is overkill for a display-only widget. An Integration Procedure adds a server round trip for data that is already local. A scheduled job introduces staleness and extra writes for a read-only need.

questions.question: An OmniScript must display data whose source of truth is an external ERP. The architect must decide how the script gets that data. Which approach is the most defensible?
options: Have the OmniScript call the ERP directly on each step
Synchronize the needed ERP data into Salesforce and read it locally
Store the ERP data in a custom setting and read it from there
Ask the user to enter the ERP data manually in the script
questions.explanation: Synchronizing the needed data into Salesforce lets the OmniScript read local copies with predictable latency and failure handling, which is the defensible enterprise pattern. Calling the ERP on each step multiplies latency and failure points. A custom setting is for configuration, not transactional data. Manual entry is error-prone and defeats the purpose of integration.
